modules.title: Design solutions that align with security best practices
modules.intro: An architect decides what to build before anyone configures it. This module covers resilience against ransomware, Microsoft's reference architectures and benchmark, Zero Trust adoption, and the Cloud Adoption and Well-Architected frameworks (about 20 to 25 percent of the exam). Meet **Harlow Lines**, an electricity distributor with 2,000 staff, control rooms and substations full of operational technology, on premises Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Azure and some AWS. Ana, its new cybersecurity architect, must design a security programme the board can fund.

lessons.title: A resiliency strategy built on critical assets
steps: Start with the business

**Business resiliency** means the business keeps running, or recovers fast, even when an attack succeeds. Ana starts by mapping key business processes, such as fault restoration and billing, to the systems behind them: apps, databases, identity systems, domain controllers and backups.
Rank threats and set targets

She ranks threats by their impact on those assets: ransomware, data theft and extortion, insider misuse and outages. For each critical process she agrees a **recovery time objective (RTO)**, how long it can be down, and a **recovery point objective (RPO)**, how much data can be lost.
Assume breach

Following the Zero Trust idea of **assume breach**, the plan covers detection, containment and recovery, not just prevention. Identity systems such as Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory are always critical, because whoever controls identity controls everything else.
Tools that help prioritise

**Microsoft Security Exposure Management** offers **critical asset management**, with built in and custom classifications such as domain controllers and sensitive databases, so attack paths and alerts touching them stand out. Defender for Cloud attack path analysis and Secure Score show which fixes cut the most risk.

check.q: Harlow Lines' board asks Ana where its resilience strategy should start. What is the right first step?
options: Deploy a new endpoint protection product everywhere
Patch every server to the latest version
Map critical processes to their assets
Run a penetration test of the public website
check.why: Resilience starts from what the business cannot lose, so the first step is identifying critical processes and their supporting assets, then setting RTO and RPO. Tools, patching and tests matter, but without priorities they are not aimed at what matters most.

lessons.key: A resiliency strategy starts with critical business assets, ranks threats by impact, sets RTO and RPO, and plans for breach.

lessons.title: BCDR and secure backup across hybrid and multicloud
steps: Two halves of BCDR

**Business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR)** has two halves. **Azure Backup** keeps data safe and restorable, covering Azure VMs, databases in VMs, files, blobs and disks, plus on premises servers through the MARS agent or Azure Backup Server. **Azure Site Recovery** keeps workloads running by replicating VMs and servers to another region or into Azure, with recovery plans and test failovers.
Matching tools to targets

Backup alone means a longer RTO. Replication gives a short RTO but also copies corruption or encryption, so point in time backups are still needed. Ana pairs Site Recovery for the outage management system with daily backups.
Backups attackers cannot destroy

**Soft delete** keeps deleted backup data recoverable, **immutable vaults** block deleting recovery points or cutting retention (and once locked, cannot be undone), and **multi user authorisation** requires permission on a separate **Resource Guard**, owned by the security team, for critical operations.
Isolation and testing

Backups need separate credentials and subscriptions, ideally a Resource Guard in a different tenant, protected domain controller backups and recovery documents. Restores must be tested regularly, because an untested backup is a hope, not a plan.

check.q: Harlow Lines replicates its outage system to a second region with Site Recovery. Why does Ana still require point in time backups?
options: Site Recovery cannot replicate Azure VMs
Backups give a shorter RTO than replication
Replication only works for on premises servers
check.why: Replication mirrors changes, including ransomware encryption or corruption, so clean point in time backups are still needed. Site Recovery does replicate Azure VMs, replication gives the shorter RTO, and it works for Azure as well as on premises.

lessons.key: Combine Azure Backup for data and Site Recovery for running workloads, and protect backups with soft delete, immutability, MUA and regular restore tests.

lessons.title: Ransomware protection in priority order
steps: Human operated ransomware

**Human operated ransomware** is a hands on attack: criminals get in, steal credentials, move sideways, escalate privilege, often steal data for extortion, then encrypt critical systems. It is far more dangerous than automated commodity malware.
Step 1: prepare recovery

Microsoft orders the work by priority. First, **prepare a recovery plan** that takes away the attacker's bargaining power: back up critical systems including Active Directory, protect backups with immutability or offline copies, protect recovery documents and test recovery so it meets the agreed times.
Step 2: limit the damage

Second, **limit the scope of damage** by protecting privileged roles so one compromise cannot reach everything: secure admin workstations, unique local admin passwords, controls against privilege escalation and Conditional Access for admin sessions.
Step 3: make entry hard

Third, **make it hard to get in**: patch internet facing systems, require MFA, protect email, enable attack surface reduction rules (audit first, then block) and replace exposed admin access with Bastion or application proxies. This step never ends, so it must not delay steps one and two.

check.q: Ana's team wants to spend the first six months only on hardening email and endpoints against ransomware. What does Microsoft's guidance say?
options: Agree, because preventing entry always comes first
Spend the time on detection rules instead
Focus only on backups and nothing else
Recovery and privileged access come first
check.why: Microsoft prioritises preparing recovery and limiting damage through privileged access, because entry hardening never finishes. Leading with prevention, detection or backups alone leaves gaps the guidance specifically warns about.

lessons.key: Ransomware defence goes recovery plan first, then protecting privileged access, then making entry hard, without letting step three delay the others.

lessons.title: Evaluating security update solutions
steps: Every asset needs a path

A good update design covers every kind of asset and gives one view of compliance. Ana lists Harlow's Windows and Linux servers in Azure, on premises and in AWS, staff laptops and phones, and the OT systems that cannot be patched on a normal schedule.
Servers

**Azure Update Manager** patches Windows and Linux servers in Azure and, through **Azure Arc**, on premises and in other clouds. It assesses machines every 24 hours, installs in customer defined maintenance windows, and supports **hotpatching** some Windows Server VMs without reboots.
Clients

**Windows Autopatch** automates Windows quality and feature updates, drivers and Microsoft 365 Apps, Edge and Teams updates for client devices in rings, managed through **Intune**, which also offers its own update policies.
Prioritising

**Defender Vulnerability Management** and Defender for Cloud rank missing updates by exposure and exploitability. Internet facing VPNs and appliances are patched fastest, because ransomware crews exploit them. Systems that cannot be patched are isolated or replaced.

check.q: Harlow Lines needs one service to schedule patching for Windows and Linux servers in Azure, on premises and in AWS. What should Ana recommend?
check.why: Update Manager covers servers in Azure and, through Arc, on premises and in AWS, with maintenance windows and assessment. Autopatch and Intune rings target client devices, and site by site tools give no single cloud view.

lessons.key: Use Azure Update Manager (with Arc) for servers, Windows Autopatch and Intune for clients, and Defender Vulnerability Management to prioritise.

lessons.title: The Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures
steps: What MCRA is

The **Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures (MCRA)** are a set of diagrams showing end to end security based on Zero Trust across legacy IT, multicloud, IoT, operational technology and AI. They are part of Microsoft's Security Adoption Framework.
What it contains

MCRA shows Microsoft's security capabilities across identity, endpoints, apps, data, infrastructure and security operations, plus views for Zero Trust user access, the SOC, OT and multicloud. **Attack chain coverage** maps products such as Defender for Office 365, Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Identity to attack stages, so gaps are visible.
How architects use it

Ana uses MCRA as a starting template for Harlow's target architecture, to compare current tools with recommended capabilities, to find integration points with existing third party tools, and to explain capabilities to executives.
MCRA versus MCSB

MCRA describes what capabilities fit where. The **Microsoft cloud security benchmark** describes what controls to configure. Architects use both: MCRA for the shape of the solution, MCSB for the settings.

check.q: Ana wants to show executives which attack stages Harlow's current products cover and where gaps remain. Which resource fits best?
options: A Defender for Cloud secure score report
check.why: MCRA's attack chain view maps products to attack stages, showing coverage and gaps in a way executives can follow. MCSB lists controls to configure, secure score measures configuration, and the business scenarios plan adoption rather than show coverage.

lessons.key: MCRA shows which Microsoft capabilities fit where in a Zero Trust architecture, including attack chain coverage, while MCSB says what to configure.

lessons.title: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark
steps: Concrete controls

The **Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB)** gives concrete security controls with implementation guidance for Azure, AWS and GCP, mapped to frameworks such as CIS, NIST SP 800-53 and PCI DSS. Control IDs combine a domain and number, such as NS-1 for network security.
Control domains

Domains include network security (NS), identity management (IM), privileged access (PA), data protection (DP), asset management (AM), logging and threat detection (LT), incident response (IR), posture and vulnerability management (PV), endpoint security (ES), backup and recovery (BR) and DevOps security (DS). Version 2, in preview, adds an AI domain.
How it is applied

Defender for Cloud enables MCSB by default for Azure, AWS and GCP, and its recommendations feed secure score and the compliance dashboard. Microsoft also publishes per service **security baselines** that apply MCSB to individual services such as Key Vault.
What mappings mean
A mapping shows a feature helps meet a requirement, not that you are fully compliant. Ana uses MCSB as the baseline for Harlow's landing zones and every new workload.

check.q: Ana needs a cloud agnostic set of security controls with Azure, AWS and GCP guidance to baseline Harlow's landing zones. What should she use?
check.why: MCSB provides concrete controls with Azure, AWS and GCP guidance and framework mappings. MCRA shows capabilities rather than settings, the Zero Trust framework plans adoption, and the cost pillar is about spending.

lessons.key: MCSB provides concrete, multicloud security controls grouped by domain, applied by default in Defender for Cloud and through per service baselines.

lessons.title: Insider, external and supply chain attacks
steps: External attacks

**External attacks** come through phishing, credential theft and exposed services. Controls include phishing resistant MFA and Conditional Access, Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Endpoint, Defender XDR for correlated detection, and Exposure Management to close attack paths.
Insider risk

**Insider risk** comes from trusted people misusing access, on purpose or by accident, such as a departing engineer copying network diagrams. Controls include **Purview Insider Risk Management** (pseudonymised by default), communication compliance, data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, least privilege, PIM, access reviews and separation of duties.
Supply chain attacks

**Supply chain attacks** compromise a trusted supplier: a software update, an open source package, a build pipeline or a service provider's privileged access. Controls include a **software bill of materials (SBOM)**, dependency scanning, protected pipelines with workload identity federation instead of secrets, and signed artefacts.
Partner access

Third party access is limited and monitored: granular delegated admin for Microsoft 365 partners, B2B guests with Conditional Access and access reviews. Harlow's SCADA vendor gets time limited, monitored access through Private Access rather than a standing VPN account.

check.q: Harlow Lines worries that a compromised open source library in its billing app could reach production. Which control most directly addresses this?
check.why: Inventorying and scanning dependencies in the build pipeline catches vulnerable or malicious packages before release. Insider risk targets staff behaviour, MFA protects accounts, and Safe Links protects email links, none of which inspect third party code.

lessons.key: Design for external attacks with identity and XDR, insider risk with Purview and least privilege, and supply chain risk with SBOMs, secure pipelines and controlled partner access.

lessons.title: AI security in the MCSB
steps: Three pillars

The MCSB **AI domain** groups controls into **AI platform security** (protect models, training data and infrastructure), **AI application security** (protect prompts, orchestration and plugins from injection and leakage) and **monitor and respond**.
Controls AI-1 to AI-4

**AI-1** use only approved models that passed verification. **AI-2** apply layered content filtering on input, intermediate processing and output, such as Azure AI Content Safety and Prompt Shields. **AI-3** use safety system instructions that resist jailbreaks. **AI-4** apply least privilege to agent tools and plugins.
Controls AI-5 to AI-7

**AI-5** keep a human in the loop for critical actions. **AI-6** monitor for jailbreaks, prompt injection, anomalies and data exfiltration, for example with Defender for Cloud threat protection for AI services. **AI-7** run continuous AI red teaming with tools such as PyRIT.
At Harlow

Harlow is building an outage assistant that can draft customer notices and create work orders. Ana requires an approved model, content filters, an agent identity with least privilege, human approval before any work order is issued, and Defender monitoring.

check.q: Harlow's outage assistant can create field work orders. Which MCSB AI control requires a person to approve those actions?
options: AI-1 Ensure use of approved models
AI-5 Ensure human in the loop
check.why: AI-5 requires human approval for critical actions. Approved models, red teaming and content filtering are all important controls, but none of them puts a person in front of the action.

lessons.key: The MCSB AI domain covers approved models, layered filtering, safety instructions, least privilege for agents, human approval, monitoring and red teaming.

lessons.title: The Zero Trust adoption framework
steps: Principles
**Zero Trust** rests on three principles: **verify explicitly** using all signals, **use least privilege access**, and **assume breach** by segmenting, encrypting and detecting.
Business scenarios

The **Zero Trust adoption framework** turns those principles into business led plans. Its scenarios are: rapidly modernise your security posture (usually the start), secure remote and hybrid work, identify and protect sensitive business data, prevent or reduce damage from a breach, and meet regulatory and compliance requirements.
The adoption lifecycle

Each scenario moves through **define strategy** (the business case), **plan**, **ready**, **adopt** in increments, **govern** by tracking progress, and **manage** by monitoring and maturing. Technology pillars include identities, endpoints, data, apps, infrastructure, network and security operations.
RaMP

The **Rapid Modernization Plan (RaMP)** is a prioritised checklist of quick wins, such as explicitly validating trust for all access requests, ransomware recovery readiness and data protection. Ana uses RaMP to show the board early results while the longer scenarios progress.

check.q: Harlow's board wants visible Zero Trust progress within a quarter. Which part of Microsoft's guidance gives a prioritised checklist of quick wins?
options: The Cloud Adoption Framework strategy guide
check.why: The Rapid Modernization Plan is a prioritised checklist built for fast Zero Trust results. Hunting queries, MCRA diagrams and the CAF strategy guide are useful, but none is a quick win plan.

lessons.key: The Zero Trust adoption framework uses business scenarios and a strategy to manage lifecycle, with RaMP providing prioritised quick wins.

lessons.title: A strategy for secure AI adoption
steps: Governance first

Secure AI adoption starts with **governance**: an AI centre of excellence sets responsible AI policies and approved tools, and staff get sanctioned AI tools and training so they do not turn to unapproved shadow AI.
Discover risks

The Cloud Adoption Framework's AI guidance has three steps. **Discover** AI security risks by extending threat modelling with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP generative AI risks, assessing data risk, testing for prompt injection and data leakage, and red teaming.
Protect and detect

**Protect** AI resources and data: inventory AI assets with Defender for Cloud AI security posture management (part of Defender CSPM), use managed identities and private networking, classify data with Purview and prevent leakage with DLP. **Detect** threats with AI posture recommendations, Defender for AI Services alerts and AI specific incident response plans.
Finding shadow AI

Defender for Cloud Apps catalogues generative AI apps in use, Purview DSPM for AI shows sensitive data in prompts, and agents get identities through Entra Agent ID. Ana finds staff using three unapproved chatbots and replaces them with a sanctioned Copilot rollout.

check.q: Ana wants an inventory of every AI workload across Harlow's Azure and AWS accounts, with misconfigurations and attack paths. Which capability fits?
options: Defender for Cloud Apps Cloud Discovery
check.why: AI security posture management in Defender CSPM discovers AI workloads across clouds with their misconfigurations and attack paths. Cloud Discovery finds SaaS AI apps users visit, DSPM for AI covers data in prompts, and Secure Score covers Microsoft 365 posture.

lessons.key: Secure AI adoption starts with governance, then discovers, protects and detects AI risks using posture management, identity, Purview and Defender for AI.

lessons.title: CAF and WAF security and governance strategy
steps: Cloud Adoption Framework

The **Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)** guides the whole cloud journey through strategy, plan, ready, adopt, govern, secure and manage. Its **secure** methodology applies from the start, covering security posture modernisation, incident preparedness, the CIA triad and sustaining posture, aligned with Zero Trust.
CAF govern

CAF's **govern** methodology builds a governance team, assesses cloud risks, documents policies, enforces them, preferably automatically with Azure Policy, management groups and RBAC, and monitors compliance.
Well-Architected Framework

The **Azure Well-Architected Framework (WAF)** is the workload level counterpart, with five pillars: reliability, security, cost optimisation, operational excellence and performance efficiency. Architects balance trade offs between them, such as extra inspection adding cost and delay.
The security checklist

WAF's security checklist runs from SE:01 (a security baseline) through secure development, data classification, segmentation, identity, network control, encryption, hardening, secrets, monitoring and testing, to SE:12 (incident response). The **Well-Architected Review** assesses a workload against it, and Azure Advisor gives recommendations.

check.q: Ana must review one new workload, the customer outage portal, against security best practice. Which framework is designed for that level?
check.why: The Well-Architected Framework works at workload level, with a security checklist and review tool. CAF and the Zero Trust scenarios work at estate and organisation level, and MCRA describes capabilities rather than reviewing a workload.

lessons.key: CAF guides estate wide adoption, security and governance, while WAF's security pillar and checklist assess individual workloads.

lessons.title: Recommending governance solutions and landing zones
steps: Turning frameworks into solutions

Governance in practice uses **Azure Policy** (deny, audit, modify, deployIfNotExists and initiatives assigned at management group scope), **management groups** for inheritance, **Azure RBAC** with PIM, resource locks, **Defender for Cloud** posture, Azure Advisor, Azure Resource Graph for inventory and cost management with tagging.
What a landing zone is
An **Azure landing zone** is CAF's ready output: a secure, scalable foundation built across design areas such as identity, resource organisation, networking, security, management and governance.
Management group hierarchy

The reference hierarchy has an intermediate root for broad policies, a **platform** group with identity, management and connectivity subscriptions, a **landing zones** group with **corp** (private) and **online** (internet facing) children, plus **sandbox** and **decommissioned**. Keep it flat, and use subscriptions rather than management groups for environments.
Platform and application landing zones

A central platform team runs shared services such as domain controllers, Sentinel and the hub firewall. Workload teams own application landing zones. **Subscription vending** creates pre governed subscriptions, and policy enforces security by default. Harlow's new outage portal lands in an online landing zone with policies inherited automatically.

check.q: Harlow wants every new subscription to inherit security policies automatically. Where should Ana assign the core policy initiatives?
options: On each resource after it is deployed
On each subscription when it is created
In the sandbox management group only
check.why: Assigning initiatives at management group scope means every subscription placed beneath inherits them automatically. Per resource or per subscription assignment depends on someone remembering, and the sandbox group does not cover production.

lessons.key: Govern with Azure Policy, RBAC and Defender for Cloud assigned through a landing zone management group hierarchy, so new subscriptions inherit controls.

lessons.title: DevSecOps aligned with CAF
steps: Security owned by developers too

**DevSecOps** makes security continuous and shared by developers, often called shift left, while still assuming breach and measuring time to detect and recover. It follows Microsoft's **Security Development Lifecycle**.
Plan, develop, build

Plan with security requirements and **threat modelling**. Develop with secure coding and pre commit secret checks. Build with **static analysis (SAST)**, secret scanning with push protection, dependency scanning with an SBOM, infrastructure as code scanning and container image scanning, for example through GitHub Advanced Security and the Microsoft Security DevOps extension.
Deploy and operate

Deploy with protected branches, approvals, least privilege service connections and **workload identity federation** instead of stored secrets, with secrets in Key Vault and policy gates. Operate with **dynamic testing (DAST)**, penetration testing, Defender for Cloud and Sentinel.
Defender for Cloud DevOps security

**DevOps security** in Defender for Cloud connects Azure DevOps, GitHub and GitLab. Foundational CSPM shows code, secret, IaC and dependency findings. Defender CSPM adds pull request annotations and **code to cloud** mapping, linking a running resource to the code that deployed it.

check.q: Harlow's pipelines store cloud credentials as long lived secrets. What should Ana require instead?
options: Secrets kept in a protected variable group
A certificate stored with each pipeline
check.why: Workload identity federation lets pipelines exchange their own tokens for Entra tokens, so no secret exists to leak. Protected variables, rotated secrets and stored certificates are improvements, but they are still credentials that can be stolen.

lessons.key: DevSecOps builds threat modelling, SAST, secret and dependency scanning, IaC scanning and federated pipeline identity into every stage, visible in Defender for Cloud DevOps security.

modules.title: Design security operations, identity and compliance
modules.intro: This module covers how Harlow Lines will detect and respond to attacks, how people, partners, workloads and agents get access, how privileged access is protected, and how regulations become controls (about 25 to 30 percent of the exam). As a regulated electricity distributor with critical infrastructure duties, Harlow needs designs Ana can defend to auditors as well as attackers.

lessons.title: Detection and response with XDR and SIEM
steps: What XDR is

**XDR (extended detection and response)** uses deep telemetry from Microsoft's own protection products, correlated automatically into incidents, with built in response actions. **Microsoft Defender XDR** covers endpoints, email, identity, cloud apps and Defender for Cloud alerts.
What a SIEM adds

A **SIEM** ingests logs from almost anything (firewalls, Linux, AWS, SaaS, line of business apps), runs your own analytics rules, keeps data for long periods and supports compliance reporting. **Microsoft Sentinel** is the cloud native SIEM, with a data lake tier for cheap long term storage.
The recommended pattern

Turn on Defender XDR for Microsoft workloads, connect it to Sentinel, and onboard Sentinel to the **Defender portal** so one incident queue spans both. Use Sentinel for third party sources and detections that need data XDR does not have.
Cost design

Alerts and incidents from Microsoft Defender products are free to ingest into Sentinel, while raw advanced hunting tables are billed. Ana sends Harlow's OT sensor alerts and firewall logs to Sentinel, and keeps Defender endpoint raw data in XDR unless hunts need it longer.

check.q: Harlow Lines needs detection across Microsoft 365, its OT firewall logs and AWS CloudTrail in one incident queue. What should Ana design?
options: XDR and Sentinel unified in the Defender portal
check.why: XDR gives deep Microsoft coverage and Sentinel ingests the firewall and AWS data, with the Defender portal unifying incidents. XDR alone cannot ingest those logs, Sentinel alone loses XDR's native depth, and separate consoles give no single queue.

lessons.key: Pair Defender XDR for deep Microsoft coverage with Sentinel for everything else, unified in the Defender portal.

lessons.title: Centralised logging and Purview Audit
steps: Questions a logging design answers

A logging design decides what to collect, where to store it, how long to keep it and who can read it. Ana starts with Harlow's regulatory retention duties and the sources investigators need most: sign ins, admin actions, endpoint and OT alerts.
Few workspaces

Microsoft recommends as few **Log Analytics workspaces** as possible. Extra workspaces are justified by data residency, separate billing, different retention or strict separation, and resource context and table level access control should be tried before splitting.
Purview Audit

**Microsoft Purview Audit** is the Microsoft 365 unified audit log. **Audit (Standard)** is on by default and keeps 180 days. **Audit (Premium)** keeps key records for a year, adds custom retention policies and forensic insights. Ten year retention needs Premium plus an add on, and is not retroactive.
Bringing it together

For correlation and long retention, Microsoft 365 activity can be streamed into Sentinel, and Entra sign in and audit logs sent there through diagnostic settings. Harlow keeps sign in logs for seven years using Sentinel's data lake tier.

check.q: Harlow's lawyers want Microsoft 365 audit records kept for ten years. What is required?
options: Audit (Premium) with custom one year policies
Audit (Premium) plus the ten year add on
check.why: Ten year retention needs Audit (Premium) and the add on licence, and applies only from when the policy is set. Premium alone keeps a year, Standard keeps 180 days, and a workspace does not change Purview retention.

lessons.key: Keep workspaces few, use Purview Audit Standard or Premium for Microsoft 365 records, and stream key logs to Sentinel for correlation and long retention.

lessons.title: Monitoring hybrid and multicloud environments
steps: Two layers
Hybrid and multicloud monitoring has two layers: **posture and protection**, and **log collection**. Both should end up in the same tools so the SOC sees one picture.
Posture and protection

Defender for Cloud connects AWS accounts and GCP projects through native connectors. Non Azure servers are projected into Azure with **Azure Arc**, so Defender for Servers and Azure Policy apply. Defender for Containers covers EKS and GKE clusters.
Log collection

Windows and Linux machines send logs with the **Azure Monitor Agent** and data collection rules. Network appliances send Syslog or CEF to a Linux forwarder. AWS logs such as CloudTrail and VPC flow logs come through the S3 connector, GCP through Pub/Sub connectors, and SaaS through Defender for Cloud Apps and vendor connectors.
Many tenants

Service providers and groups with several tenants use **Azure Lighthouse** and Sentinel's multi tenant management. Harlow has a separate tenant for its retail energy subsidiary, which Ana's SOC monitors through multi tenant management in the Defender portal.

check.q: Harlow wants its on premises and AWS EC2 servers covered by Defender for Servers and Azure Policy. What should Ana include?
options: Azure Arc for the non Azure servers
check.why: Arc makes non Azure servers Azure resources so Defender for Servers and Azure Policy both apply. A workspace adds logging, AWS tools do not apply Azure Policy, and direct onboarding gives Defender coverage but loses Azure Policy and machine configuration.

lessons.key: Monitor hybrid and multicloud with Defender for Cloud connectors and Arc for posture, and AMA, forwarders and cloud connectors for logs.

lessons.title: Designing SOAR with Sentinel and Defender XDR
steps: Why automate
**SOAR** (security orchestration, automation and response) reduces analyst effort and time to contain. Harlow's SOC is small, so automation is part of the design, not an afterthought.
Sentinel automation

**Automation rules** run in order when incidents or alerts are created or updated. Without code they assign owners, change status or severity, add tags and task lists, close noise and run playbooks. **Playbooks** are Logic Apps that call APIs: open a ticket, block an IP, post to Teams or disable a user.
Permissions

Sentinel's service account needs Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on a playbook's resource group before automation rules can run it, and analysts need Playbook Operator to run playbooks by hand.
Defender XDR automation

**Automated investigation and response** investigates alerts and proposes or takes remediation, depending on automation level. **Automatic attack disruption** contains in progress attacks such as ransomware with high confidence. Ana's rule of thumb: built in XDR actions first, automation rules for routing and hygiene, playbooks only for cross system orchestration.

check.q: Ana wants every confirmed phishing incident to open a ticket in Harlow's IT service system and notify the duty manager in Teams. What should handle that?
options: An automation rule that assigns the incident
A playbook run by an automation rule
A Defender XDR alert tuning rule
check.why: Cross system actions such as opening tickets and posting to Teams need a playbook, triggered by an automation rule. An automation rule alone cannot call external systems, analytics rules detect rather than act, and tuning rules suppress alerts.

lessons.key: Use XDR's built in response first, Sentinel automation rules for routing and hygiene, and Logic App playbooks for cross system orchestration.

lessons.title: Incident response, hunting and incident management
steps: The incident response lifecycle

Incident response follows **preparation** (playbooks, roles, contacts, emergency procedures, out of band communication), **detection and analysis**, **containment, eradication and recovery**, and **post incident activity**, where lessons feed new detections and controls.
Incident management in the tools

The Defender portal gives one queue for XDR and Sentinel incidents. Analysts assign owners, set status and severity, use tasks for standard steps and **classify** incidents when closing so tuning data is captured. Playbooks connect to IT service management, and Security Copilot summarises incidents and drafts reports.
Major incidents

For major incidents Microsoft stresses separate roles (incident lead, investigators, communications), protecting privileged accounts first, and assuming the attacker can read normal email, so Harlow keeps an out of band channel ready.
Threat hunting

**Threat hunting** assumes something slipped past detections. Hunters start from a **hypothesis**, query advanced hunting across XDR and Sentinel tables, investigate and bookmark findings, then turn reliable logic into detection rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Finding nothing but adding a detection is still a success.

check.q: During a major ransomware incident at Harlow, why does Ana insist on an out of band communication channel?
options: Email delivery is too slow during incidents
The attacker may read normal email
Teams cannot be used for incidents
check.why: Microsoft's guidance assumes the attacker may have access to normal channels, so responders coordinate somewhere the attacker cannot see. Speed, audit rules and Teams licensing are not the reason.

lessons.key: Design incident response across preparation to lessons learned, manage incidents in one queue with classification, and run hypothesis driven hunts that end in detections.

lessons.title: Evaluating detection coverage with MITRE ATT&CK
steps: Tactics and techniques
**MITRE ATT&CK** is a public catalogue of real attacker behaviour. **Tactics** are goals, such as initial access or lateral movement. **Techniques** are methods, such as credential dumping.
Three matrices

The **Enterprise** matrix covers Windows, macOS, Linux, cloud, network devices and containers. **Mobile** covers Android and iOS. **ICS** covers industrial control systems, with tactics such as inhibit response function and impair process control. Harlow needs all three.
Measuring coverage

Sentinel's MITRE ATT&CK page shows **active** coverage from enabled rules and **simulated** coverage from templates not yet enabled. Rules, hunting queries and bookmarks are tagged with techniques. Product coverage maps too: Defender for Endpoint for Enterprise, mobile threat defence for Mobile, and Defender for IoT for ICS.
Prioritising gaps

Gaps are prioritised by threat intelligence relevant to the sector, not by trying to fill every cell. Ana focuses first on ICS techniques seen in attacks on power utilities, then on enterprise techniques used by ransomware groups.

check.q: Ana wants to check detection coverage for Harlow's substation control systems. Which MITRE ATT&CK matrix applies?
check.why: The ICS matrix covers industrial control systems and operational technology. Mobile covers phones and tablets, and Enterprise covers IT systems but not ICS specific tactics.

lessons.key: Evaluate coverage with ATT&CK's Enterprise, Mobile and ICS matrices, using Sentinel's active and simulated views, and prioritise gaps by sector threat intelligence.

lessons.title: Designing agent identities
steps: Agents need governed identities
AI agents act on data and systems, so they need identities governed like users and apps. **Microsoft Entra Agent ID** provides them.
Building blocks

An **agent identity blueprint** is a template for a kind of agent. It holds the credentials and gets tokens for its agents, so admins can disable or apply policy to every agent of that kind at once. An **agent identity** is a service principal created from a blueprint, with no credentials of its own. An optional **agent user account** serves systems that need a user. A **sponsor** is the accountable person or group.
Conditional Access for agents

For app only calls, policies target agent identities or the **blueprint**, which also covers future agents. For on behalf of calls, user policies apply. Agent users are not covered by all users policies and must be targeted separately. Typical policies block agents at high risk.
Limits

Conditional Access cannot help if an agent uses an **API key** instead of Entra tokens. Ana therefore requires Harlow's outage assistant to use its agent identity for every call, with API keys disabled on the resources it uses.

check.q: Harlow will create dozens of field agents from one design. How can Ana apply one Conditional Access policy to all current and future agents of that kind?
options: List each agent identity by name
check.why: Targeting the blueprint covers every agent created from it, including new ones. Named lists miss future agents, all users policies do not cover agent identities, and workload identity targeting is a different mechanism.

lessons.key: Entra Agent ID uses blueprints, agent identities, optional agent users and sponsors, and Conditional Access can target blueprints but not API key access.

lessons.title: Access to SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, on premises and multicloud
steps: Centralise on Entra ID
Zero Trust access design centralises authentication and policy in **Microsoft Entra ID**, so Conditional Access applies everywhere. Every separate identity store is a separate attack surface.
SaaS and Azure

SaaS apps join through the Entra gallery with SAML or OpenID Connect single sign on, SCIM provisioning for account lifecycle, and Defender for Cloud Apps for discovery and session control. Azure resources use **Azure RBAC** for management and data roles where supported, with **managed identities** for workloads.
On premises apps

**Microsoft Entra Private Access** replaces VPNs with per app access to any TCP or UDP app, and **application proxy** publishes on premises web apps. Both bring Conditional Access and MFA to legacy apps, with Kerberos delegation through the connector.
Multicloud

AWS IAM Identity Center and Google Cloud are federated with Entra ID using SAML and SCIM, so the same identities, MFA and access reviews apply. Harlow's AWS engineers now sign in with their Entra accounts instead of separate AWS users.

check.q: Harlow's engineers have separate local user accounts in AWS. What should Ana design instead?
options: Keep local accounts but enforce MFA in AWS
Use AWS IAM users with access keys
Share one administrator role per team
check.why: Federation with SAML and SCIM brings AWS access under Entra identities, Conditional Access and access reviews. Local accounts with MFA remain a separate identity store, access keys are long lived secrets, and shared roles remove accountability.

lessons.key: Centralise access in Entra ID: gallery SSO and SCIM for SaaS, RBAC and managed identities for Azure, Private Access for on premises, and federation for other clouds.

lessons.title: Entra ID for hybrid environments
steps: Sync options

**Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync** uses light agents with configuration in the cloud, several agents for availability, and handles **disconnected forests**. **Microsoft Entra Connect Sync** is the full server based engine, needed for features such as merging attributes across forests, rich filtering and very large groups. Both can run side by side during migration.
Password hash sync

**Password hash synchronisation** syncs a hash of the password hash and authenticates in the cloud. It is the simplest and most resilient method and enables leaked credential detection. Microsoft recommends it, at least as a backup.
Pass-through and federation

**Pass through authentication** validates passwords on premises through agents, so on premises policies apply, but outages affect cloud sign in. **Federation with AD FS** is the most complex and a target for forged token attacks, so Microsoft recommends moving to cloud authentication with **staged rollout**.
Protecting the bridge

The sync server, AD FS and related systems belong to the control plane (Tier 0) and must be protected as strongly as domain controllers. Harlow moves from AD FS to password hash sync and decommissions its federation servers.

check.q: Harlow still federates sign in through an ageing AD FS farm. What does Microsoft recommend Ana design?
options: Add more AD FS servers for resilience
Move to password hash sync via staged rollout
Keep AD FS and add a WAF in front
check.why: Microsoft recommends migrating from AD FS to cloud authentication, preferably password hash sync, using staged rollout. Pass through still depends on on premises agents, and adding AD FS servers or a WAF keeps the federation attack surface.

lessons.key: Choose Cloud Sync or Connect Sync by feature needs, prefer password hash sync, migrate off AD FS with staged rollout, and protect sync servers as Tier 0.

lessons.title: External identities and decentralised identity
steps: B2B collaboration

**B2B collaboration** invites partners as **guest users** who sign in with their own identity provider. **B2B direct connect** creates mutual trust without guest objects, mainly for Teams shared channels, and is blocked by default.
Cross tenant access

**Cross tenant access settings** control inbound and outbound collaboration by default and per partner, trust partners' MFA and device claims so guests are not prompted twice, and support cross tenant synchronisation. **Tenant restrictions v2** controls which outside tenants Harlow's users may sign in to. Guests are governed with entitlement management and access reviews.
Decentralised identity

In **decentralised identity**, an **issuer** gives a person a signed **verifiable credential**, the **holder** keeps it in a wallet such as Microsoft Authenticator, and a **verifier** checks the signature without calling the issuer each time. **Microsoft Entra Verified ID** issues and verifies these credentials.
Use cases

Verified ID helps remote onboarding (verify an ID before issuing a Temporary Access Pass), help desk recovery (require a credential, optionally with Face Check, before resets) and partner access packages that require an employed by credential. Harlow uses it to stop social engineering at its help desk.

check.q: Attackers keep phoning Harlow's help desk pretending to be staff who lost their phones. Which design best stops this?
options: A Verified ID credential with Face Check
A one time code sent to the caller's email
A call back to the number the caller gives
check.why: A verifiable credential plus liveness matching proves identity far better than knowledge questions. Managers' names are easy to research, and codes or call backs to contact details the caller supplies can be controlled by the attacker.

lessons.key: Govern partners with B2B, cross tenant settings and access reviews, and use Entra Verified ID credentials for strong identity proofing.

lessons.title: Modern authentication and authorisation
steps: Conditional Access building blocks

Conditional Access evaluates when a token is issued: assignments (users, roles, agents, workload identities), conditions (risk, device, location, client app) and controls (block, MFA, **authentication strength**, compliant device, app protection, session limits). It needs P1, and risk conditions need P2.
Authentication strengths and context

Built in strengths are multifactor, passwordless and **phishing resistant** (FIDO2 keys, Windows Hello for Business and multifactor certificates). **Authentication context** labels sensitive resources, such as a labelled SharePoint site or a PIM activation, so stricter policy applies only there.
Continuous access evaluation

**Continuous access evaluation (CAE)** lets services such as Exchange, SharePoint, Teams and Graph react within minutes to critical events: account disabled, password reset, sessions revoked or high user risk. They also enforce IP based locations instantly, so tokens can live longer safely.
Risk scoring and protected actions

**ID Protection** scores sign in and user risk. Recommended policies require risk remediation for high user risk and MFA for medium or high sign in risk, in separate policies. **Protected actions** require an authentication context when admins change Conditional Access, named locations or cross tenant settings, or hard delete objects.

check.q: Ana wants any admin who edits a Conditional Access policy to have just completed phishing resistant MFA, regardless of how they got their role. What should she design?
options: Sign in frequency of one hour for admins
A protected action with authentication context
A named location for the admin team
check.why: Protected actions enforce an authentication context at the moment of sensitive operations, whatever role grants them. Sign in frequency and named locations apply at sign in, and PIM approval applies at activation, not at each sensitive change.

lessons.key: Modern access design combines Conditional Access with authentication strengths and context, CAE for fast revocation, risk policies, and protected actions for sensitive admin changes.

lessons.title: Validating Conditional Access against Zero Trust
steps: A persona based framework

Microsoft's Zero Trust guidance recommends organising Conditional Access by **persona**: global, admins, internal users, guests, workload identities and agents, with consistent naming so gaps are easy to spot.
Baseline policies

Ana checks for policies that block legacy authentication, require MFA or a strength for all users, require **phishing resistant MFA** for admins, require compliant or hybrid joined devices for corporate resources, apply user and sign in risk, secure security info and device registration, and restrict unknown platforms and high risk countries.
Validation techniques
She uses **What If** to simulate sign ins, **report only** mode before enforcement, the insights workbook, and sign in log queries for sign ins where no policy applied or legacy clients were used.
Exclusions

Only emergency access accounts should be broadly excluded, and exclusion groups need access reviews. The Conditional Access optimisation agent in Security Copilot can flag users and apps not covered by baselines. At Harlow she finds a contractors group excluded from MFA two years ago and never reviewed.

check.q: Ana wants to find sign ins that no Conditional Access policy covered at all. What is the most direct method?
options: Query sign in logs for not applied
Run What If for every user
check.why: Sign in logs record each sign in's Conditional Access result, so filtering for not applied reveals uncovered sign ins directly. Secure Score and assignment reviews show intent, not actual coverage, and What If for every user is impractical.

lessons.key: Validate Conditional Access by persona baselines, What If, report only mode, sign in log queries and strict review of exclusions.

lessons.title: Hardening Active Directory Domain Services
steps: Write requirements, not clicks
An architect specifies AD DS hardening as measurable requirements. Ana groups Harlow's into privileged accounts, credentials, protocols and configuration, and monitoring and recovery.
Privileged accounts and credentials

Keep Domain Admins and similar groups nearly empty, use separate Tier 0 admin accounts, add them to **Protected Users**, and allow admin logons only from privileged workstations. Use **Windows LAPS** for unique local admin passwords, **group managed service accounts** for services (resisting Kerberoasting), and rotate the krbtgt account periodically and twice after compromise.
Protocols and configuration

Reduce NTLM and remove SMBv1, enforce SMB and LDAP signing and channel binding, fix unconstrained delegation, weak permissions and old stored passwords in Group Policy, and remove vulnerable **AD Certificate Services** templates.
Monitoring and recovery

Deploy **Defender for Identity** sensors on domain controllers, AD FS, AD CS and Entra Connect servers, and review its identity posture assessments in Secure Score. Keep offline or immutable domain controller backups and a tested forest recovery plan.

check.q: Harlow's service accounts use short passwords that never change, and attackers could request their tickets to crack offline. What should Ana require?
options: Adding the accounts to Protected Users
Moving the accounts into Domain Admins
Forcing the accounts to use RC4
check.why: gMSAs use long, automatically rotated passwords that resist Kerberoasting. Protected Users is for interactive privileged users and breaks many services, Domain Admins raises the impact, and RC4 makes cracking easier.

lessons.key: Harden AD DS with minimal Tier 0 accounts, Protected Users, LAPS, gMSAs, protocol hardening, AD CS fixes, Defender for Identity and tested forest recovery.

lessons.title: Designing secrets, keys and certificates management
steps: Choosing the service

**Key Vault Standard** stores software protected keys, secrets and certificates. **Premium** adds HSM backed keys in a shared service. **Managed HSM** is a dedicated single tenant HSM pool with its own security domain and local RBAC that subscription owners cannot override, suited to strict key custody requirements.
Design rules

Use one vault per application, environment and region to limit blast radius. Use **Azure RBAC** for data access, with roles such as Key Vault Secrets User for apps. Soft delete is always on, and **purge protection** should be enabled, as many customer managed key scenarios require it.
Network and identity
Disable public access and use private endpoints. Apps authenticate with **managed identities**. Logs go to Log Analytics, and Defender for Key Vault detects unusual access.
Rotation and discovery

Key rotation policies, certificate auto renewal with integrated CAs and Event Grid near expiry events drive automation. **Secret scanning** in GitHub Advanced Security finds hard coded secrets. Harlow's regulator requires that only Harlow can access its encryption keys, so Ana chooses Managed HSM.

check.q: Harlow's regulator requires single tenant HSMs whose access even Azure subscription owners cannot override. Which service should Ana choose?
check.why: Managed HSM provides dedicated single tenant HSMs with its own security domain and local RBAC. Standard and Premium are multitenant services governed by Azure RBAC, and config files are not a key store.

lessons.key: Choose Key Vault Standard, Premium or Managed HSM by key custody needs, with one vault per app, RBAC, purge protection, private endpoints and automated rotation.

lessons.title: Privileged role design with the enterprise access model
steps: Planes of control

Microsoft's **enterprise access model** replaces the old tier model. The **control plane** (expanded Tier 0) covers identity and access for the whole enterprise: Global Administrator, domain controllers, Entra Connect, AD FS, AD CS, PIM and Conditional Access. The **management plane** covers enterprise wide IT management. The **data and workload plane** covers per app administration. **User access** and **app access** cover employees, partners, customers and APIs.
The golden rule
Lower planes must never control higher planes. A workload admin must never be able to reset a control plane admin's password or edit a Tier 0 Group Policy object.
Delegation

Use the narrowest built in roles, such as Helpdesk Administrator, and **administrative units** to scope by region, rather than Global Administrator. Use **PIM** for just in time elevation, separate cloud only admin accounts used only from privileged workstations, and two or more emergency access accounts.
Azure

In Azure, assign at management group or subscription scope only when truly needed, and delegate resource group scope to workload teams. Ana gives Harlow's regional IT teams Helpdesk Administrator scoped to their region's administrative unit.

check.q: A Harlow workload admin can edit a Group Policy object that applies to domain controllers. Why is this a design flaw?
options: A lower plane controls a higher plane
Workload admins should be Global Administrators
Domain controllers do not use Group Policy
check.why: The enterprise access model forbids lower planes from controlling higher ones, and domain controllers are control plane assets. Group Policy is still used, and giving workload admins more power makes it worse.

lessons.key: The enterprise access model separates control, management, workload and access planes, and lower planes must never control higher ones.

lessons.title: Evaluating Entra ID governance and access reviews
steps: PIM

**PIM** removes standing privilege with **eligible** assignments activated just in time, using MFA or authentication context, justification and approval, for Entra roles, Azure roles and groups. PIM controls activation, while Conditional Access and protected actions protect the use of a role.
Entitlement management

**Entitlement management** bundles groups, apps and sites into **access packages** in catalogs, with request policies, approval stages, expiry, separation of duties and connected organisations for partners, whose guests are removed when their last assignment ends.
Access reviews

**Access reviews** check group and app access, access package assignments and privileged roles. Design choices include reviewers (owners, managers, self), scope (all, guests or inactive users), recurrence, decision helpers and **auto apply** of results. Native reviews cover Entra integrated resources, and other systems need custom reviews or third party tools.
Licensing

P2 covers PIM, core access reviews and basic entitlement management. **Entra ID Governance** adds lifecycle workflows, custom extensions, Verified ID in packages, automatic assignment, machine learning assisted and inactive user reviews. New governance features arrive in ID Governance. Review history provides audit evidence for frameworks such as ISO 27001.

check.q: Harlow wants joiner and leaver tasks automated from HR dates, such as issuing a Temporary Access Pass before day one. Which licence does that need?
check.why: Lifecycle workflows are an Entra ID Governance feature. P2 covers PIM and core reviews but not lifecycle workflows, P1 lacks them too, and Workload ID Premium is for service principals.

lessons.key: Evaluate governance through PIM for just in time roles, entitlement management for packaged access, and access reviews, with advanced features in Entra ID Governance.

lessons.title: Active Directory attack resilience
steps: Credential reuse attacks

**Pass the hash** and **pass the ticket** reuse cached credentials to move between machines. Mitigations are tiered logon restrictions, Credential Guard, Windows LAPS, Protected Users and never using Tier 0 accounts on workstations.
Kerberos attacks

**Kerberoasting** requests service tickets for accounts with service names and cracks them offline: use gMSAs or very long passwords with AES only. **AS-REP roasting** targets accounts without Kerberos pre authentication: require it. A **Golden Ticket** forges tickets with the krbtgt key: protect domain controllers and reset krbtgt twice after compromise.
Replication and certificate abuse

**DCSync** and **DCShadow** abuse replication rights: restrict them to domain controllers and detect with Defender for Identity. Misconfigured **AD CS** templates let attackers request certificates as any user: review templates and enrolment rights.
Governance and recovery

Review privileged groups and **lateral movement paths** shown in Defender for Identity, track identity posture in Secure Score, and keep offline domain controller backups and a documented forest recovery plan. Harlow's tabletop exercise reveals no one has practised a forest recovery, so Ana schedules one.

check.q: After a suspected Golden Ticket attack, what must Harlow do with the krbtgt account?
check.why: Forged tickets are signed with the krbtgt key, so resetting it twice invalidates them. It cannot be deleted, adding it to groups is meaningless, and forged tickets can be made with long lifetimes.

lessons.key: Design AD resilience against pass the hash, Kerberos, replication and AD CS attacks, with Defender for Identity monitoring and practised forest recovery.

lessons.title: Secure administration of tenants, SaaS and multicloud, and CIEM
steps: Microsoft 365 and Entra

Use **cloud only** accounts for Entra privileged roles so an on premises compromise cannot take over the cloud. Keep fewer than five Global Administrators and at least two emergency accounts protected with FIDO2 and monitored. Use PIM, phishing resistant MFA for admins and protected actions, and review high privilege app consents.
Azure, SaaS and other clouds

In Azure use management groups, least privilege RBAC, PIM for Owner and User Access Administrator, policy guardrails and Activity logs into Sentinel. Federate AWS and Google Cloud admin access to Entra ID and avoid AWS root and long lived keys. Use Defender for Cloud Apps SaaS posture management for apps such as ServiceNow, and granular delegated admin for partners.
What CIEM is

**Cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM)** closes the gap between permissions granted and permissions used: an AWS role with full access, a GCP service account with Owner, an Azure service principal with Contributor. It discovers identities and entitlements across clouds, compares them with activity, and recommends removing inactive or overprovisioned access.
Which product

Microsoft Entra Permissions Management has been retired, and Microsoft now recommends **Defender CSPM** for CIEM, where overprovisioned identities also appear in attack paths. Ana pairs CIEM findings with PIM for Azure roles and time bound federated access in AWS.

check.q: Ana needs CIEM for Harlow's Azure and AWS identities. What does Microsoft currently recommend?
options: Defender CSPM in Defender for Cloud
check.why: Entra Permissions Management has been retired, and Microsoft recommends Defender CSPM's CIEM capabilities. LAPS and Site Recovery solve different problems.

lessons.key: Administer tenants with cloud only, PIM protected, phishing resistant admin accounts, and use Defender CSPM's CIEM to right size multicloud permissions.

lessons.title: Privileged access workstations and secure remote administration
steps: Device security profiles

Microsoft defines **enterprise** devices for normal productivity, **specialised** devices with no local admin and only approved apps, and **privileged access workstations (PAW)** for roles whose compromise would seriously harm the organisation.
PAW requirements

A PAW blocks email and general browsing, allows only listed sites, is managed by Intune with baselines and Defender for Endpoint, deployed with Autopilot, enforces application control, gives no local admin, and uses TPM, Secure Boot, Credential Guard and BitLocker. Admins use a separate device or account for everyday work.
Enforcing PAW use

A Conditional Access policy with a **device filter** or compliant device requirement for admin roles makes sure admin sign ins come only from PAWs, combined with PIM authentication context and protected actions. Hardened Windows 365 Cloud PCs can serve where physical PAWs are impractical.
Remote administration

**Azure Bastion** gives browser or native client access to VMs without public IPs, with session recording on Premium. **Just in time VM access** opens management ports briefly for approved users. **Private Access** gives per app access to RDP or SSH targets on premises. Harlow's control system admins work only from PAWs through Private Access.

check.q: How can Ana make sure Harlow's Global Administrators can only sign in from privileged access workstations?
options: Require phishing resistant MFA for admins
A policy asking admins to use PAWs
A device filter policy for admin roles
check.why: A Conditional Access device filter or compliance requirement for admin roles technically enforces PAW use. Phishing resistant MFA and PIM protect the account but not which device it is used from, and a written policy cannot enforce anything.

lessons.key: Admins use hardened PAWs enforced by Conditional Access device filters, and reach servers through Bastion, just in time access or Private Access.

lessons.title: Turning compliance requirements into controls
steps: What versus how

A regulation says what, such as protect customer data or keep logs of access. The architect designs how. Ana inventories Harlow's obligations: privacy law, energy sector security rules, ISO 27001 and contracts.
Mapping and responsibility

Obligations are mapped to a control framework such as MCSB or Compliance Manager templates. Under the **shared responsibility model**, some controls are Microsoft's (physical security), some are Harlow's (MFA, classification) and some are shared.
Technical controls

Data residency becomes an Azure Policy allowed locations rule. Encryption becomes customer managed keys. Access logging becomes Purview Audit and diagnostic settings to Sentinel. Data protection becomes labels, DLP and retention. Least privilege becomes PIM and access reviews.
Testable controls and evidence

Controls must be testable: all storage accounts deny public network access can be checked, data is secure cannot. Evidence comes from Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance, Compliance Manager, audit reports and the Service Trust Portal for Microsoft's own audits.

check.q: Harlow's regulator requires customer data to stay in New Zealand and Australia. Which control expresses that requirement in Azure?
options: A sensitivity label on customer data
Customer managed keys in Key Vault
An Azure Policy allowed locations rule
check.why: Allowed locations blocks resources outside approved regions, a testable residency control. Labels, keys and DLP protect data in other ways but do not stop resources being created elsewhere.

lessons.key: Translate regulations into testable controls mapped to a framework and the shared responsibility model, with evidence from Defender for Cloud and Compliance Manager.

lessons.title: Compliance solutions with Microsoft Purview
steps: Compliance Manager

**Compliance Manager** offers many regulatory templates and custom ones to create **assessments**, each listing Microsoft managed, customer managed and shared controls. **Improvement actions** are assigned, evidenced and tracked, rolling up to a risk based compliance score.
Protecting information

**Information Protection** uses sensitivity labels for encryption and marking with auto labelling. **Data loss prevention** covers email, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and endpoints. **Data lifecycle and records management** keep or delete content with retention policies and labels.
Investigating and monitoring people

**Audit** and **eDiscovery** support investigations and legal holds. **Communication compliance** and **insider risk management** address conduct and insider threats. **DSPM for AI** covers AI related data risk.
Data across the estate

**Data Map** and the **Unified Catalog** discover and classify data across Azure, on premises and other clouds. Ana's design principle is to choose the solution that produces the required evidence and enforcement, not just visibility.

check.q: Harlow must show auditors which ISO 27001 controls are Microsoft's responsibility and which are its own, with progress tracked. Which Purview solution fits?
check.why: Compliance Manager assessments separate Microsoft, customer and shared controls and track improvement actions. eDiscovery and communication compliance serve investigations and conduct, and Data Map catalogues data.

lessons.key: Purview covers compliance tracking with Compliance Manager, protection with labels, DLP and retention, investigation with Audit and eDiscovery, and data discovery with Data Map.

lessons.title: Azure Policy and Defender for Cloud for compliance
steps: Policy building blocks

**Azure Policy** uses definitions grouped into **initiatives**, such as the MCSB or a regulatory initiative, assigned at management group, subscription or resource group scope with parameters, exclusions and time limited **exemptions** (waiver or mitigated).
Effects and design

Effects include deny, audit, modify and append, deployIfNotExists (needing a managed identity), denyAction and manual attestation. Assign guardrails at management group level, start in audit then move to deny, use remediation tasks for existing resources, and manage policies as code. Policy also reaches Arc enabled servers and AKS.
Regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud

Defender for Cloud enables MCSB automatically across Azure, AWS and GCP. Standards such as PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and NIST can be added with a qualifying paid plan, and custom standards need Defender CSPM. Each control shows passing, failing or not automatically assessable, with **manual attestation** for procedural controls.
Reporting

Compliance reports can be downloaded, exported continuously and charted in workbooks, and Defender for Cloud results can feed Compliance Manager for one view across Microsoft 365 and cloud. Neither Secure Score nor the dashboard proves certification by itself.

check.q: Some of Harlow's ISO 27001 controls are procedural, such as staff screening, and cannot be checked automatically. How should Ana record them in Defender for Cloud?
check.why: Manual attestation adds evidence for controls that cannot be assessed automatically. Deleting controls hides them, and deny policies and secure score do not evidence procedural controls.

lessons.key: Use Azure Policy initiatives at management group scope to enforce controls, and Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance, with manual attestation, to validate alignment.

modules.title: Design security solutions for infrastructure
modules.intro: Infrastructure covers posture across clouds, servers and clients, IoT and operational technology, cloud services and networks (about 25 to 30 percent of the exam). Harlow Lines has all of these: Azure and AWS workloads, on premises servers, thousands of laptops and phones, smart meters, and substations whose control systems cannot be scanned or patched like normal IT.

lessons.title: Posture with Defender for Cloud, MCSB and Secure Score
steps: Defender for Cloud

**Microsoft Defender for Cloud** combines **cloud security posture management (CSPM)**, **cloud workload protection (CWPP)** and **DevOps security**. Architects use it to answer how well configured every cloud is.
The yardstick

The **Microsoft cloud security benchmark** is the default standard. Its policies evaluate resources and produce recommendations that feed **secure score**, and the regulatory compliance dashboard shows its status. Microsoft also publishes per service security baselines.
Two secure scores

The classic **Defender for Cloud secure score** groups MCSB recommendations into controls, giving points only when all a control's recommendations are fixed, with preview ones excluded. The newer **Cloud Secure Score** in Exposure Management is risk based, weighting by risk level, asset exposure and criticality.
Microsoft Secure Score

**Microsoft Secure Score** in the Defender portal covers Entra ID, Defender products, Exchange, Teams, SharePoint and connected SaaS apps. Actions are worth up to 10 points, some partially by coverage, and can be marked planned, risk accepted or resolved through a third party or alternate mitigation. Ana reports both scores to Harlow's board each quarter.

check.q: Harlow's board asks for one number showing Microsoft 365 and identity security posture. Which score should Ana report?
options: Defender for Cloud classic secure score
check.why: Microsoft Secure Score covers Microsoft 365, identity and Defender products. Defender for Cloud's score covers cloud resources, compliance score tracks regulatory actions, and a control ID is not a score.

lessons.key: Defender for Cloud measures cloud posture against MCSB with its secure scores, while Microsoft Secure Score measures Microsoft 365 and identity posture.

lessons.title: Integrated posture, workload protection and Azure Arc
steps: One view of every environment

An integrated design brings AWS (through a connector deployed with CloudFormation or Terraform, ideally at the management account), GCP (project or organisation connectors), on premises and other cloud servers (through **Azure Arc**) and code repositories (DevOps connectors) into Defender for Cloud.
Free and paid posture

**Foundational CSPM** gives inventory, recommendations, secure score and remediation. **Defender CSPM** adds attack paths, cloud security explorer, risk prioritisation, governance rules, regulatory standards, agentless scanning, data and AI posture and code to cloud mapping. Enabling plans at management group scope covers new subscriptions.
Choosing workload protection

Choosing **CWPP** is mapping workload to plan: **Servers** (Plan 1 for Defender for Endpoint, Plan 2 adding agentless scanning, file integrity monitoring and just in time access), **Storage**, **Databases**, **Containers**, **App Service**, **Key Vault**, **Resource Manager**, **APIs** and **AI Services**. Alerts flow into Defender XDR.
Azure Arc

**Azure Arc** gives non Azure machines an Azure resource ID, RBAC and a managed identity, which brings in Defender for Servers, Azure Policy machine configuration, Update Manager and the Azure Monitor Agent. Arc is only for machines outside Azure, and AWS and GCP connectors can deploy it automatically. Arc enabled Kubernetes extends Defender for Containers.

check.q: Harlow's 40 on premises SCADA historian servers run Windows. Which design brings them under Defender for Servers and Azure Policy?
options: Treat them as Azure VMs without changes
check.why: Arc makes on premises servers Azure resources so Defender for Servers and Policy apply. They are not Azure VMs, and Office 365 protection and Autopatch do not provide server workload protection.

lessons.key: Integrate AWS, GCP, Arc enabled servers and DevOps into Defender for Cloud, choose Defender CSPM and CWPP plans by workload, and use Arc for non Azure machines.

lessons.title: External attack surface and exposure management
steps: Defender EASM

**Defender External Attack Surface Management** recreates an attacker's view from the internet. From **discovery seeds** such as domains, IP blocks and ASNs, it follows connections to find related infrastructure, including forgotten sites. Assets are labelled approved, candidate, dependency, monitor only or requires investigation, and dashboards show exposed vulnerabilities and expiring certificates.
Attack paths

The **cloud security graph** in Defender CSPM links resources, permissions, network exposure, vulnerabilities and sensitive data. **Attack path analysis** finds chains from an entry point, through lateral movement, to a critical target, with fixes that break the chain. **Cloud security explorer** lets teams query the graph proactively.
Exposure Management

**Microsoft Security Exposure Management** runs a continuous exposure management cycle: **security initiatives** for areas such as ransomware or identity with metrics, **exposure insights**, an attack surface map, attack paths with **choke points** where many paths meet, and **critical asset management**.
Attack surface reduction

**Attack surface reduction rules** in Defender for Endpoint block risky behaviours such as Office apps starting child processes, rolled out in audit then block. Ana requires a monthly process: review new external assets, break the top attack paths to critical assets and track initiative scores.

check.q: Many of Harlow's attack paths pass through one over privileged service account. What does Exposure Management call such a point, and why fix it first?
check.why: A choke point is where many attack paths converge, so fixing it removes many risks together. Seeds, candidates and dependencies are EASM inventory terms, not points where paths converge.

lessons.key: Use EASM for the outside in view, attack paths and explorer for chained risk, and Exposure Management initiatives and choke points to run a continuous posture process.

lessons.title: Server and client endpoint requirements
steps: Server requirements

A good server specification covers protection (Defender for Endpoint through Defender for Servers), vulnerability management with a patch deadline through Update Manager, an OS baseline through Azure Policy machine configuration, no public RDP or SSH (Bastion or just in time access), managed identities and LAPS, monitoring through the Azure Monitor Agent, and protected backups, applied the same way through Arc everywhere.
Corporate devices

Corporate owned phones and laptops enrol in **Intune** (for example with Windows Autopilot or Apple business enrolment), with **compliance policies** for encryption, OS version, passcodes and jailbreak detection, plus configuration profiles.
Personal devices

For personal devices, **app protection policies** protect corporate data inside apps such as Outlook and Teams without managing the whole device: block copying to personal apps, require a PIN and allow selective wipe. **Defender for Endpoint on iOS and Android** detects phishing sites and malicious apps.
Enforcement

Conditional Access enforces it all with require compliant device or require app protection policy, plus authentication strengths. Harlow's field crews use corporate phones with full enrolment, while office staff use personal phones with app protection only.

check.q: Harlow's office staff refuse to enrol personal phones but need Outlook and Teams. What should Ana require?
options: Use web access only with no controls
check.why: App protection secures corporate data inside managed apps without enrolling the device, and Conditional Access enforces it. Blocking or forcing enrolment ignores the business need, and uncontrolled web access leaves data exposed.

lessons.key: Specify servers with EDR, patching, baselines and no public admin ports, and clients with Intune compliance for corporate devices and app protection for personal ones.

lessons.title: IoT devices and operational technology
steps: IoT device requirements

Every IoT device needs a **unique identity**, ideally an X.509 certificate backed by hardware, never a shared fleet key, with secure enrolment through the IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service. Add secure defaults, signed firmware updates and network segmentation with no inbound internet access.
Monitoring devices without agents

Many devices cannot run an agent, so monitoring is network based. **Enterprise IoT** in Defender for IoT uses Defender for Endpoint network discovery to inventory printers, cameras and phones and show their vulnerabilities. The Defender for IoT micro agent is scheduled to retire, so new designs should not depend on it.
OT and ICS

Operational technology such as PLCs, HMIs and SCADA cannot tolerate scanning or agents. **Defender for IoT OT sensors** connect to a SPAN port or network tap and passively inspect industrial protocols, building an inventory, network map and vulnerability list. Analysis happens on the sensor, so only metadata leaves low bandwidth sites.
Deployment models

OT sensors can be **cloud connected** (alerts to the Defender portal and Sentinel), **locally managed** for air gapped sites, or hybrid. Ana maps detections to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS and places sensors according to Harlow's network levels, with locally managed sensors at the most isolated substations.

check.q: Ana needs visibility of PLCs in Harlow's substations without disrupting them. What should she specify?
options: Passive Defender for IoT OT sensors
Endpoint agents installed on the PLCs
Daily remote logins to check each PLC
check.why: Passive sensors on mirrored traffic give inventory and threat detection without touching fragile devices. Active scans, agents and frequent logins can disrupt PLCs or are not possible on them.

lessons.key: IoT devices need unique identities, secure updates and segmentation, and OT is monitored passively with Defender for IoT sensors, cloud connected or locally managed.

lessons.title: Endpoint baselines and Windows LAPS
steps: Choosing a baseline tool

**Intune security baselines** cover Windows, Defender for Endpoint, Edge, Microsoft 365 Apps and Windows 365, are versioned and can conflict with other profiles. The **Security Compliance Toolkit** provides Group Policy baselines with Policy Analyzer for domain joined servers. **Azure Policy machine configuration** audits Azure and Arc servers against the Azure compute baseline.
Rolling out baselines
Baselines start in audit, are tested in a pilot ring, then enforced. Defender for Endpoint security settings management can push some endpoint policies to devices not enrolled in Intune.
Why LAPS matters

If every machine shares one local admin password, one stolen hash opens the whole estate through pass the hash. **Windows LAPS**, built into supported Windows versions, gives each device a unique, rotating password.
LAPS design

Entra joined devices back up passwords to Entra ID, AD joined devices to AD, and hybrid joined devices to one of the two. AD backup can encrypt passwords and keep history, and protect the directory services restore password on domain controllers. Passwords can rotate after use. Reading them should be limited with custom roles.

check.q: Every Harlow laptop shares the same local administrator password. Which control should Ana require?
options: A password changed manually each quarter
Disabling the local admin account only on servers
check.why: LAPS gives each device its own rotating password, so one stolen hash cannot open every machine. Longer or manually changed shared passwords still let one compromise spread, and fixing servers alone leaves the laptops exposed.

lessons.key: Pick baselines by management model (Intune, Group Policy or machine configuration), roll out in audit first, and use Windows LAPS for unique local admin passwords.

lessons.title: Baselines for SaaS, PaaS and IaaS, and IoT workloads
steps: IaaS
With **IaaS** you own the operating system, middleware and network rules. The baseline covers OS hardening, patching, EDR, network security groups and disk encryption.
PaaS

With **PaaS**, Microsoft runs the operating system and you configure the service. Microsoft's per service security baselines apply MCSB controls such as network isolation, identity, data protection and logging, enforced with Azure Policy initiatives at management group scope in a landing zone.
SaaS
